facts.statement: The genus Trematosteus was first described by Gross in 1932.
Fossils of Trematosteus have been found in Bad Wildungen, Germany.
facts.quote: Fossils are found from Bad Wildungen, Germany.

facts.statement: Trematosteus lived during the Late Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
facts.quote: Trematosteus is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm from the Late Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.

facts.statement: Trematosteus is classified as an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm.
facts.quote: Trematosteus is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm

facts.statement: Trematosteus belongs to the superfamily Incisoscutoidea and the clade Coccosteomorphi.
facts.quote: Trematosteus is a member of the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: The parent group of Trematosteus is the family Trematosteidae.
Trematosteus is a member of the class Placodermi.
Trematosteus lived between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)
